summary: Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the EPHE and Paris Diderot University under supervisors including Maxime Kaltenmark, Léon Vandermeersch, and Kristofer Schipper, and held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Bordeaux.

Michela Clemente works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri, later teaching Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and literature at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).
Michele Martin (born 1942) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle C. Wang specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her doctorate under Eugene Y. Wang (~2002–2008) and was appointed assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University around 2012.

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1997–2001) and taught at Victoria University of Wellington and Colorado College.

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies specialist. He earned his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky (~1997–2002) and held an academic post at Leiden University from ~2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1974). He served at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974–1980) and professor (~1993–2016), and headed the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies in 2015.

Michihiko Yajima (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed graduate work at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Setagaya Gakuen Junior and Senior High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and worked as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her PhD under Raimon Panikkar at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1976–1983) and was a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).
Michio Kamikawa (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1998.

Michio Yano (born 1944) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and David Pingree, and was a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Michitoshi Barada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), and held posts at Otani University (1992) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (2000–2003).
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held a post at the same institution (attested 2001–2004).
Michiyo Demoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held an academic post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Michiyo Hoshi is a researcher in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa as a collaborative researcher and at Toyo Bunko as a researcher (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later served as a researcher there (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering (d. 1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey. He served as Sa skya expert at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1990) and was Head of Sakya College (attested 1991–1997).

Mihai Șora (1916–2023) was a Romanian philosopher. He studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris, and CNRS, later working at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1954–1969).
